Article Title: Scientists build a silicon chip that writes DNA with electricity, paving the way for cleaner gene synthesis and DNA-based data storage
Article Text:
Representative image

How the silicon chip works

From neuroscience to biotechnology

Potential applications

Challenges ahead

Silicon chips have long been the backbone of computing, but a Harvard-led research team has given them an entirely different job: writing DNA. As reported by Science Daily, a study published in Nature Electronics, Harvard researchers have unveiled a silicon chip DNA writer capable of synthesising DNA using electricity and water-based enzymes. The innovation marks a major departure from traditional phosphoramidite chemistry, which relies on hazardous organic solvents. The chip can simultaneously produce 64 different DNA sequences, each up to 39 nucleotides long, offering a cleaner and more scalable approach to DNA manufacturing.The project involved Harvard, the Broad Institute, DNA Script, and POSTECH, with funding from IARPA, Horizon Europe, and Samsung Research. Intellectual property has been filed by Harvard’s Office of Technology Development.The chip assembles DNA strands one nucleotide at a time. A temporary blocking group halts growth until removed under acidic conditions. By applying tiny electrical currents, the chip generates protons that lower pH locally, enabling DNA synthesis to continue. Each site is confined by concentric ring electrodes, allowing parallel construction of multiple sequences.This precise control makes the process safer and more efficient than conventional methods.Synthetic DNA is essential for diagnostics, genome engineering, and cancer research. Current methods require centralized facilities and involve toxic solvents. The Harvard chip’s water-based enzymatic process could enable portable DNA-writing devices, making the technology more accessible to labs and clinics worldwide.Interestingly, the chip’s design originated in neuroscience research, where it was used to record electrical activity in neurons. Researchers later repurposed its precision current injection technology to control chemical conditions for DNA synthesis, bridging the gap between brain science and biotechnology.* Portable DNA-writing devices for labs and hospitals* DNA data storage, demonstrated by encoding a 169-byte text* Synthetic biology and diagnostics with reduced environmental impactScaling the technology will require new chemistry. Current limitations stem from intermediate molecules drifting between synthesis sites during deprotection. Researchers are working on more direct acid-driven chemistry to overcome this hurdle, aiming for longer and more complex DNA sequences.
Article Summary: Harvard researchers have unveiled a silicon chip DNA writer capable of synthesising DNA using electricity and water-based enzymes. The innovation marks a major departure from traditional phosphoramidite chemistry, which relies on hazardous organic solvents. The chip can simultaneously produce 64 different DNA sequences, each up to 39 nucleotides long.

Article Title: US court says Meta, Google, TikTok, Snapchat must face addiction lawsuits
Article Text:
Meta also loses bid to delay multistate trial

Part of a mounting legal pattern

A US appeals court has ruled that Meta Platfoms, Google, TikTok and Snapchat must face thousands of lawsuits alleging that their platforms were designed to be addictive for young users. According to a report by Reuters, the San Francisco-based 9th US Circuit Court has rejected an appeal made by Meta and TikTok in which the companies speed to to overturn a lower court’s decision which allowed more than 3,000 federal cases to proceed. The social media giants also argued that Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act which offer shields to online platforms from liability for user content should also protect them from claims that their designs encourage addiction. The 9th Circuit disagreed with the framing entirely, ruling that Section 230 offers a defense against liability rather than outright immunity from being sued, which meant the appeal came too early in the process.The court also denied Meta’s request to delay a multistate trial brought by 29 state attorneys general, who allege the company illegally collected children’s data, designed its platforms to keep young users hooked, and misled consumers about safety.The trial is set to begin Wednesday.The decision follows a New Mexico court ruling last week that found Meta had created a public nuisance and ordered it to pay $567 million into a teen mental health fund and implement youth-safety measures.Monday's ruling lands just days after a New Mexico judge found that Meta had created a public nuisance in the state, ordering the company to pay $567 million into a teen mental health fund and to implement youth-safety measures. That followed an earlier phase of the same trial in which a jury ordered Meta to pay $375 million after finding it had misled consumers about the safety of its platforms.The federal cases now cleared to move forward are centralized before U.S. District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers in Oakland, California, and seek damages, penalties and restitution. They stem from Rogers' 2023 and 2024 orders that largely allowed the litigation to proceed, orders the companies had been appealing ever since. Attorneys Lexi Hazam and Previn Warren, who represent thousands of school districts and individuals in the federal litigation, said the ruling clears the way not only for the states' trial but also for a separate trial over school district claims scheduled for February.Beyond the federal cases, the companies also face hundreds of additional lawsuits in state courts, including roughly 3,300 consolidated in a single proceeding in California state court. In the first such case to reach a verdict, a Los Angeles jury in March found Meta and Google negligent for designing platforms that harmed young users, awarding $6 million to a young woman who said she became addicted to Instagram and YouTube as a child — a closely watched early indicator of how juries may respond to similar claims going forward.
Article Summary: The San Francisco-based 9th US Circuit Court has rejected an appeal made by Meta and TikTok in which the companies speed to to overturn a lower court’s decision which allowed more than 3,000 federal cases to proceed. The social media giants also argued that Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act which offer shields to online platforms from liability for user content should also protect them from claims that their designs encourage addiction. The 9th Circuit disagreed with the framing entirely, ruling that Section230 offers a defense against liability rather than outright immunity from being sued.

Article Title: Jeff Bezos' ex-wife MacKenzie Scott is back to writing after 13 years, says: Serially throughout August, I will publish an 80,000-word ...
Article Text:
MacKenzie Scott makes her literary comeback

MacKenzie Scott's journey from billionaire to philanthropist

MacKenzie Scott makes latest donation to a US non-profit

Philanthropist and novelist MacKenzie Scott, ex-wife of Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has now announced her return to fiction writing after more than a decade. According to a report by Forbes, in a post on her blog Scoot announced that she will serially release an 80,000-word novel titled ‘Last Days in Two Nations (A History in Eighteen Minds)" throughout the month of August. Scott published the book's title page, table of contents, character list and epigraphs over the weekend, but offered little else about the plot or characters, saying only that she hoped readers would "read and subscribe" to follow along as the novel unfolds serially over the coming weeks.For those unaware, Scott studied creative writing at Princeton University under Nobel laureate Toni Morrison, who supervised her 168-page thesis, “The Fathering Water.” Morrison later praised Scott as one of her best students and helped her secure a literary agent after graduation.The announcement marks Scott's first major return to publishing in 13 years. Her debut novel, "The Testing of Luther Albright," came out in 2005 to strong critical reception, winning an American Book Award and landing a spot on the Los Angeles Times' Best of the Year list. She followed it with a second novel, "Traps," in 2013, which she promoted through a series of interviews at the time.Since then, Scott has largely stayed out of public view, surfacing only occasionally through literary posts on her blog and personal website.Once ranked as the 22nd richest person in the world, Scott has given away more than $26 billion over the past seven years to over 2,500 organizations, including historically Black colleges and universities, environmental groups, and economic equity nonprofits. According to Forbes, her current net worth stands at $33.8 billion, stemming from the 4% Amazon stake she received following her 2019 divorce from Bezos.Recently, Scott donated $20 million to Active Minds, a US nonprofit that works with young people to change the culture around mental health. The donation is the largest in the organisation's history and comes as Scott continues her large-scale charitable giving after selling a significant portion of her Amazon shares over the years. As stated in the Fortune report, the latest gift is unrestricted, allowing the nonprofit to decide how the money should be used to expand mental health programmes, support young leaders and respond to community needs.
Article Summary: The announcement marks Scott's first major return to publishing in 13 years. Her debut novel, "The Testing of Luther Albright," came out in 2005 to strong critical reception. Scott has given away more than $26 billion over the past seven years to over 2,500 organizations.

Article Title: Meta, OpenAI, Google and other AI companies are learning from your chats. Here's how to stop it
Article Text:
Google warns Blackstone, Bridgewater, Bain Capital, KKR, TPG, Moody's targeted by hackers

Why Google Gemini, ChatGPT, Meta AI and others ‘reading’ your Chat matters

How to change privacy settings on ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Grok, Meta AI and other AI platforms

ChatGPT (OpenAI)

Open ChatGPT.

Click your profile icon.

Go to Settings.

Open Data Controls.

Turn off Improve the model for everyone (or disable Chat History & Training, depending on the version you're using).

Once disabled, future chats are generally excluded from model training, although OpenAI may still retain conversations for a limited period for abuse monitoring. Existing conversations are not automatically deleted.

Google Gemini

Visit your Google Account.

Open Data & Privacy.

Select Gemini Apps Activity.

Pause activity if you don't want prompts stored for future use.

Also review Web & App Activity, Search History , and Auto-delete settings to limit long-term retention.

Users should remember that even with activity paused, Google may temporarily retain conversations for security and abuse prevention.

Meta AI (Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp)

Open Accounts Center.

Navigate to Privacy.

Review Meta AI settings where available.

Adjust public profile visibility.

Limit who can view public posts and photographs.

Use available objection or opt-out forms for AI training where applicable in your region.

Because Meta's controls vary by geography and product, users should periodically revisit these settings after major app updates.

Claude (Anthropic)

Open Claude.

Go to Settings.

Open Privacy or Data Controls.

Disable participation in model improvement if the option appears for your account.

Business and Team plans typically receive stronger default privacy protections than consumer accounts.

Grok (xAI)

Open X.

Go to Settings and Privacy.

Open Privacy and Safety.

Review AI-related data sharing settings.

Limit personalised data sharing where available.

Avoid posting confidential or sensitive information in Grok conversations. Because X frequently updates its settings menus, users should check these options after major platform updates.

Microsoft Copilot

Open Copilot.

Visit Settings.

Review Privacy and Personalisation options.

If signed into a Microsoft account, review connected account privacy settings through your Microsoft Privacy Dashboard.

Five habits matter more than any setting

Most people worry about what an AI chatbot tells them. Far fewer think about what they are telling the chatbot. Whether it's ChatGPT helping draft emails, Gemini summarising documents, Meta AI answering questions on Instagram , Claude analysing files, or Grok explaining breaking news on X, users routinely paste personal conversations, work documents, financial details and even medical queries into AI systems. In many cases, those interactions may also be used to improve future AI models unless users actively opt out.The good news is that almost every major AI company now offers some level of control over whether your conversations are used for training. The bad news is that these controls are rarely front and centre, differ significantly across platforms, and sometimes apply only to certain products or account types.Privacy experts say users should stop assuming that AI services are private by default. Instead, they should treat AI settings the same way they treat browser privacy settings or app permissions: something worth reviewing every few months.Generative AI companies rely heavily on user interactions to improve their models. Conversations help them identify errors, refine responses, improve safety systems and better understand how people actually use their products.Companies insist that they employ safeguards such as removing personally identifiable information where possible, limiting employee access, and allowing users to opt out in many cases.Enterprise and paid business offerings generally provide stronger privacy guarantees than consumer versions.Still, many people unknowingly share information they would never post publicly — salary negotiations, legal contracts, customer databases, medical histories, source code and family conversations.The simplest rule is one that cybersecurity professionals have repeated for years: never upload anything to an AI assistant that you would not be comfortable storing on someone else's cloud server.OpenAI allows users to stop new conversations from being used to improve its models through the Chat History & Training setting.How to change it:Google's AI products draw heavily from your Google Account settings. Activity is primarily controlled through Gemini Apps Activity, alongside broader account controls such as Web & App Activity.How to change it:Meta increasingly integrates AI across Facebook, Instagram and Messenger. Public posts and interactions may contribute to AI development in some regions, while users can manage several AI-related controls.How to change it:Anthropic offers relatively straightforward data controls and gives many users the option to exclude conversations from model improvement.How to change it:Grok operates inside X, making privacy settings closely tied to the X platform.How to change it:Microsoft says consumer Copilot conversations may be used to improve services, while commercial Microsoft 365 Copilot operates under enterprise privacy commitments.How to change it:Privacy specialists say changing a few settings is only part of the solution. The biggest factor in protecting personal information is still how people use AI services. They advise treating chatbots like any other cloud-based service and thinking carefully before sharing sensitive information. That means never pasting passwords, one-time passwords (OTPs), banking details or other financial credentials into an AI assistant. Users should also avoid uploading confidential workplace documents unless their employer has explicitly approved the use of AI tools. Where possible, names, addresses and other personally identifiable information should be removed before sharing text for summarisation or analysis. Experts also recommend periodically deleting conversation history if it is no longer needed and revisiting privacy settings whenever AI companies introduce major new features or update their data policies, as defaults and controls can change over time.
Article Summary: How to change privacy settings on ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Grok, Meta AI and other AI platforms. Privacy experts say users should stop assuming that AI services are private by default. Instead, they should treat AI settings the same way they treat browser privacy settings or app permissions.

What to do

Steps to follow

Many insured employees only realise they need their ESIC card when they're already standing in a queue, and by then, tracking it down often means calling HR or waiting on an employer who may be slow to respond. The fix is simpler than most people realise: the e-Pehchan card can be downloaded directly by the employee, in advance, through the Umang app Under the ESI Act, insured workers and their dependents are entitled to medical and cash benefits, but accessing that care at an ESIC hospital or dispensary requires proof of coverage. Since the card can be pulled up as a PDF on a phone, keeping a saved copy removes this friction entirely, well before it becomes a problem.The e-Pehchan card can be downloaded either through the ESIC Insured Person portal or through the Umang app, a central government platform that bundles access to services like ESIC, EPF passbook checks, gas cylinder bookings and more into a single app.For most employees, Umang is the quicker route since it doesn't require remembering separate ESIC portal credentials.1.Open the Umang app or ESIC services on the portal. Article Title: Elon Musk shares video of SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket part crashing into Moon, later issues a clarification
Article Text:
Elon Musk

Fake video viral explosion versus real science

South Korean satellite confirms Lunar impact site

What NASA administrator Jared Isaacman said

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk reposted an AI-generated video claiming to show a discarded SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket stage crashing into the Moon’s surface, before clarifying nearly an hour later that the footage was fake. However, despite the lack of live video streams, orbital spacecraft and ground observatories confirmed the impact. The actual collision occurred on August 5 when a 4,000-kilogram second-stage booster slammed into the far side of the Moon at a velocity of roughly 8,700 kilometres per hour.Musk reshared an 11-second synthetic animation created by social media accounts depicting a bright explosion and a 100-foot crater forming on the lunar surface. The clip garnered tens of thousands of likes and thousands of reposts before Musk added a brief follow-up note acknowledging, “This is fake btw”, accompanied by a laughing emoji.Space tracking experts and astrophotographers quickly flagged the video, noting that no real-time optical cameras were positioned to capture a live video feed of the impact.While live video was impossible, space agencies successfully documented the event.The Korea Aerospace Research Institute (KARI) announced that its lunar orbiter, Danuri, conducted eight imaging passes over the target area beginning 30 minutes before the calculated collision time.KARI released before-and-after imagery showing localised terrain darkening, disturbed lunar regolith and ejected material caused by the kinetic impact. The agency noted that its dataset will be paired with follow-up observations from NASA 's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) to analyse structural changes to the lunar crust.Additionally, astronomers at the Institute of Astrophysics of Andalusia (IAA-CSIC) in Spain captured remote observations from an Earth-based observatory, recording a brief plume of ejected material rising along the lunar limb.NASA’s administrator Jared Isaacman noted the agency will use part of the rocket for setting up a base on the moon.“Well, we're going to leverage reusable rockets to build the Moon base. Now, vehicles like Falcon 9, what ULA has, what Blue Origin is building, you know, Rocket Lab, they're helpful for a lot of the initial infrastructure, but then you've got the heavy lift vehicles like what Starship is capable of doing, which is fully reusable, and the new Glenn rocket that's coming. That's what allows you to put lots of mass on the surface of the Moon,” he said, as per Mashable.In another tweet he said: “For those interested in a spent booster impacting the lunar surface, this rare occurrence has decades of history, going back to the Apollo era, when NASA intentionally crashed spent stages into the Moon for science and seismic research. The reality is that meteoroids strike the lunar surface hourly, with impacts comparable to this upper stage occurring roughly every six days.”“The future lunar base will incorporate reusable spacecraft that not only deliver astronauts and payloads but also become part of the infrastructure itself,” he concluded.
Article Summary: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk reposted an AI-generated video claiming to show a discarded SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket stage crashing into the Moon’s surface. Despite the lack of live video streams, orbital spacecraft and ground observatories confirmed the impact. The actual collision occurred on August 5 when a 4,000-kilogram second- stage booster slammed into the far side of the Moon.

Article Title: Intel files $15 billion stock offering to fund AI infrastructure expansion
Article Text:
Intel shares declined after announcing a $15 billion stock offering, with proceeds aimed at supporting AI-related growth, capital expenditure, working capital and balance-sheet strength.

Funding physical AI and next-gen packaging

Strong revenue momentum drives capital outlays

Intel announced a massive $15 billion common stock offering as the chipmaker seeks to raise fresh capital to meet surging global demand for artificial intelligence (AI) processors and advanced foundry capacity. The equity raise includes a 30-day option allowing underwriters to purchase up to an additional $2.25 billion in common stock, potentially pushing total gross proceeds above $17 billion, as per CNBC.The report says that Intel management stated that net proceeds from the offering will support general corporate purposes, including working capital and heavy capital expenditures across its domestic manufacturing facilities. The chipmaker also highlighted physical AI applications, custom purpose-built silicon and advanced semiconductor packaging as primary growth drivers behind the capital push.The move comes amid a broader industry-wide infrastructure land grab. Wall Street analysts at Goldman Sachs project global capital expenditures on AI hardware and data centers will hit $765 billion this year before expanding to $1.2 trillion by 2027.This surge is said to be driven by heavy procurement from cloud giants like Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet.The multi-billion-dollar equity offering follows Intel’s recent quarterly earnings report, where the firm posted its fastest revenue growth in nearly 15 years. the results have been prompted by packed order books as Intel raised its full-year capital expenditure forecast to $20 billion. Intel CFO David Zinsner confirmed that the bulk of the outlay is directed toward advanced factory tooling, noting that the manufacturer is preparing for a "meaningful increase" in production scaling heading into 2027.Intel’s market position has been strengthened over the past year by rising commercial chip demand and strategic backing from the U.S. government, which acquired a 10% equity stake in the company to secure domestic supply chain independence. Following the early morning announcement, Intel shares dipped 4 percent in early trading as financial markets absorbed the short-term share dilution.
Article Summary: Intel announced a massive $15 billion common stock offering as the chipmaker seeks to raise fresh capital to meet surging global demand for artificial intelligence (AI) processors and advanced foundry capacity. The equity raise includes a 30-day option allowing underwriters to purchase up to an additional $2.25 billion in common stock.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Mark Cuban: “It’s not about money or connections — it’s the willingness to outwork and out-learn everyone…” - a lesson on what success really takes
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Mark Cuban

“It’s not about money or connections — it’s the willingness to outwork and out-learn everyone… And if it fails, you learn from what happened and do a better job next time.”

Understanding the meaning of the quote

What Cuban means by ‘outwork and out-learn’

All about Mark Cuban

From internet entrepreneur to billionaire investor

The lessons hidden inside a business setback

What happens after money and connections open the door

How technology is changing what workers need to learn

Success is often explained through money, opportunity or knowing the right people. Those factors can make a difference, but they do not necessarily determine what happens after a plan goes wrong. In business and in working life, people regularly have to make decisions with incomplete information, deal with setbacks and adjust when an expected result does not arrive. What happens next can matter as much as the original decision. Mark Cuban has often spoken about that part of the process, drawing attention to the value of sustained effort and the ability to keep learning. His view is particularly clear when he discusses failure: rather than treating it as the end of an attempt, he argues that it can provide information that helps shape a better decision the next time around.The wording points towards two different ideas that are easy to separate but harder to practise together.The first is effort. Cuban’s point is not simply that working long hours automatically produces good results. Hard work without direction can just mean spending more time on the wrong problem.The more useful distinction is between being willing to put in the work and expecting resources, status or personal contacts to do the work for you.Then comes learning. Someone can work relentlessly and still repeat the same mistakes. Learning changes that equation because it turns experience into something useful. A failed product, a lost customer or a bad business decision can become information about what needs to change.That makes the final part of the quote important. Failure is not presented as the objective. It is an event that has to be examined carefully, understood honestly and used to make the next decision wiser, rather than simply repeated in a different form.There is a subtle difference between the two words.To outwork someone suggests persistence. It can mean spending more time preparing, making another attempt when the first one does not succeed, answering the difficult email, learning the unfamiliar software or staying with a problem after the obvious solution has failed.To out-learn someone is different. It means paying attention to what happened while doing the work.A person who works hard but refuses to change course can remain stuck. Someone who learns but never applies that knowledge can have the opposite problem. Cuban’s phrasing places the two together: effort creates experiences, while learning determines what is done with those experiences.That is particularly relevant in business, where plans rarely survive contact with customers exactly as they were imagined. A product may be technically sound but poorly timed. A promising market may prove smaller than expected. A partnership might look sensible on paper and turn out to be difficult in practice.The useful response is not simply to work harder at repeating the original plan.Mark Cuban became widely known as an entrepreneur and investor, but his career did not begin with the kind of business empire for which he later became recognised.Born in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, in 1958, Cuban developed an early interest in business and technology. He attended Indiana University, where he studied management. After university, he worked in a number of roles before moving towards the technology industry.His early career included work in software sales. He eventually founded MicroSolutions, a computer systems company that was sold to CompuServe in 1990. That deal gave Cuban the financial base for much larger ventures.Cuban and fellow entrepreneur Todd Wagner founded AudioNet, an internet broadcasting company that later became Broadcast.com. The business grew during the late 1990s, when online broadcasting was still developing and the commercial possibilities of the internet were being tested in real time. Yahoo acquired Broadcast.com in 1999 in a deal worth billions of dollars.That transaction changed Cuban’s financial position, but it did not mark the end of his involvement in business. He moved into a collection of industries, including entertainment, sports and media.In 2000, Cuban purchased the Dallas Mavericks. The basketball team became one of the most visible parts of his public profile, while his business interests continued to expand beyond sport.He also became a television personality through Shark Tank, where entrepreneurs pitch businesses to a panel of investors. The programme gave audiences a closer view of the questions that sit behind a business idea: how much does it cost, who will buy it, what makes it different and whether the people running it understand their own numbers?Failure can be uncomfortable because it produces information that people may not want to hear.A business owner might discover that customers do not value the feature they spent months developing. A manager might realise that a hiring decision was wrong. An investor can find that an apparently attractive opportunity had risks that were underestimated. The natural temptation is to explain the outcome away.Cuban’s quote suggests a different response: investigate the result and use it to improve the next attempt.That requires separating the emotional experience of failure from the practical information it provides. Losing money hurts. Missing a target can be embarrassing. Seeing a competitor succeed with an idea that did not work for you can be particularly difficult.The answer might reveal a mistake in timing, pricing, execution, communication or judgement. Sometimes the answer is simply that the idea was not good enough.The quote should not be read as suggesting that money or relationships are irrelevant.Capital can give a business more time to develop. A strong professional network can provide access to customers, employees, investors or advice that would otherwise be difficult to obtain. Experience and reputation can make certain conversations easier.Those advantages are real, but resources do not remove the need to execute. A well-funded company can still make poor decisions. A person with an extensive network can still build something nobody wants. Connections may secure the meeting, but they cannot necessarily produce a good product or keep customers interested.That distinction is important because it makes the quote less about rejecting privilege or resources and more about what happens after those resources are available.The idea takes on a different shape in a labour market where technology can alter jobs and industries quickly.Automation, artificial intelligence, remote collaboration and new digital tools are changing how many organisations operate. Some skills become more valuable, while others can be performed faster through software.For workers, that creates a practical challenge. Experience remains useful, but experience alone can become outdated.Someone who learned one system ten years ago cannot necessarily rely on knowing that system forever. The ability to learn a replacement may matter more than the original knowledge.This is where Cuban’s distinction between effort and learning becomes relevant again. Working harder can help a person keep up for a while. Learning how the environment itself has changed can determine whether they remain useful within it.
Article Summary: Mark Cuban says failure can provide information that helps shape a better decision the next time around. He argues that effort creates experiences, while learning determines what is done with those experiences. Failure is not presented as the objective. It is an event that has to be examined carefully, understood honestly and used to make the next decision wiser.

Article Title: Microsoft may launch its next AI chip next month to challenge Nvidia dominance
Article Text:
Expanding custom silicon manufacturing with TSMC

Accelerating silicon development cycles

Microsoft is preparing to unveil its next-generation custom artificial intelligence (AI) processor, the Maia 300, as early as next month, a report has said. Article Title: Quote of the day by Henry Ford: Even a mistake may turn out to be the one thing necessary to a worthwhile achievement
Article Text:
What Henry Ford said about mistakes

Why Henry Ford's quote about mistakes matters

“Failure is simply the opportunity to begin again, this time more intelligently.”

Henry Ford believed mistakes could sometimes contribute to achievement. His quote, “Even a mistake may turn out to be the one thing necessary to a worthwhile achievement,” reflects the idea that an error can become part of the process leading to a meaningful result. The quote is attributed to Ford, the American industrialist who founded Ford Motor Company and died in 1947.The statement suggests that mistakes should not always be viewed only as setbacks. In some situations, an error can provide information, reveal a different approach or lead to changes that contribute to an eventual achievement. Ford's quote has been reproduced in educational and professional materials discussing learning from mistakes and experience.Henry Ford was an American industrialist associated with the development of automobile manufacturing and the Ford Motor Company. He was born on July 30, 1863, and died on April 7, 1947.His statement about mistakes connects errors with the possibility of reaching a worthwhile achievement. Rather than describing mistakes as an automatic path to success, the quote points to situations where an unsuccessful attempt can become necessary to reaching a desired outcome.The quote is also included in educational material from The Henry Ford, which lists it among Ford's statements on achievement, possibility and failure.The quote focuses on what can follow a mistake rather than the mistake itself. An error can expose a problem in an existing method, provide information about what does not work or lead someone to reconsider an approach.This idea has also appeared in material about learning from experience. A mathematics textbook, for example, uses Ford's quote while discussing why making mistakes can be part of the learning process.Ford is also attributed with other statements about failure and learning, including the line,Together, these statements present mistakes and failure as experiences that can provide information for subsequent attempts. The quote in the headline similarly places a mistake within the broader process of working towards an achievement, rather than treating every error as the end of that process.

Article Title: Rogue AI models of Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta that went on hacking other companies had a common 'Israel link'
Article Text:

Irregular says issue came from same test environment

Why the incidents matter

AI models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta recently made headlines after they accessed websites and systems they were not supposed to during security testing. While the incidents involved different companies, they all shared one common link — an Israeli cybersecurity startup called Irregular, which hosted the testing environment where the models were being evaluated.Over the past two weeks, OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta each disclosed that one of their AI models accessed websites that should have been off-limits during internal cybersecurity tests. The companies all pointed to Irregular, a three-year-old startup based in Tel Aviv, Israel, which hosted the evaluation test environment used for the security checks.ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said in a blog post that a misconfiguration in Irregular's testing environment allowed its AI model to access the public internet. Similarly, Claude-maker Anthropic said it informed Irregular after discovering that its Claude model may also have reached the internet during testing. Meta later said it learned about a similar incident from Irregular and is investigating what happened.Irregular told CNBC that all three incidents were caused by the "same evaluation-environment issue" first disclosed by Anthropic. The company said the incidents did not involve an AI escaping its testing environment or carrying out a sophisticated cyberattack.It also said there are currently no unresolved issues and that it is preparing a white paper on best practices for secure AI cybersecurity testing.The disclosures have renewed attention on how advanced AI models are tested before release. During these evaluations, AI systems are intentionally asked to find software weaknesses or security gaps in controlled environments. Experts told CNBC that companies often rely on independent firms like Irregular instead of testing their own AI systems to ensure unbiased evaluations.Sundeep Bhimireddy, head of AI at enterprise startup Von, said AI developers do not want to "grade their own homework," making third-party testing important.

Article Title: FCC issues public notice on foreign-made drones with LiDAR obstacle-avoidance features, says they pose an 'unacceptable risk' to national security
Article Text:
Besides LiDAR, the proposal also covers foreign-made drones on the Covered List

LiDAR-equipped drones could be affected

FCC seeks to expand earlier drone ban

Other drone features also included

The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has issued a public notice proposing to ban the import and sale of certain foreign-made drones equipped with LiDAR obstacle-avoidance technology, saying such drones pose an "unacceptable risk" to US national security. The proposal could remove several popular consumer drone models from US stores if it is approved. The notice, published in the Federal Register on August 3, seeks public comments until September 2, 2026. If adopted, the new restrictions would take effect about 180 days after publication.One of the main technologies targeted is LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging), which uses laser pulses to measure distances and create detailed 3D maps. The technology is widely used in drones for obstacle avoidance and safer flying.If the proposal is approved, consumer drones such as DJI's Air 3S and Mini 5 Pro, which use LiDAR for obstacle detection, could no longer be imported or sold in the United States. The proposed rule would not affect people who already own these drones, although manufacturers have warned that official spare parts could become harder to obtain over time.The proposal builds on an FCC decision made in December 2025, when the agency added all foreign-made drones and their critical components to its Covered List. Equipment on the list is considered by US national security authorities to pose an "unacceptable risk." That earlier move blocked new foreign-made drone models from receiving FCC authorization needed for sale in the US. However, models that had already received approval before the ban were still allowed to be imported and sold.The latest proposal aims to close that gap by retroactively removing sales approval for previously authorised drone models that include what the FCC calls "military-grade" features.Besides LiDAR, the proposal also covers foreign-made drones on the Covered List that include thermal imaging sensors, agricultural spraying systems, docking stations, defence-related equipment, weigh 55 pounds or more, or can operate in coordinated swarms. The FCC said the proposal is based on national security concerns and believes the economic impact would be limited because such drones represent only a small part of the overall consumer drone market.
Article Summary: FCC seeks to ban the import and sale of certain foreign-made drones equipped with LiDAR obstacle-avoidance technology. The proposal could remove several popular consumer drone models from US stores if it is approved. If adopted, the new restrictions would take effect about 180 days after publication. The FCC said the proposal is based on national security concerns.

Article Title: Melbourne man asked his AI assistant to book a gym class, and it went on to hack the gym; it is the assistant that Sam Altman spent millions on to ...
Article Text:
Disclaimer: It is an AI-generated image

How OpenClaw managed to hack the gym

Sam Altman’s investment in OpenClaw

Broader sisks of AI agents

Legal and policy questions

A Melbourne man named Andrew asked his AI assistant to book him a spot in a coveted morning gym class. What seemed like a simple task quickly escalated when the AI discovered a vulnerability in the gym’s booking software. According to a report by ABC News, the assistant not only booked classes months in advance — beyond the system’s limits — but also removed another gym-goer from the waitlist to move Andrew up. Shocked, Andrew said he never asked the AI to hack the system.As per the report, Andrew was experimenting with OpenClaw, a popular AI agent software powered by Anthropic’s Claude AI. It is the same assistant in which OpenAI CEO Sam Altman spent millions on. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman hired developer Peter Steinberger and his open-source AI agent project, OpenClaw (formerly Clawdbot) for millions in a talent grab. AI agents combine chatbot abilities with tools to access the internet, email, and multi-step planning. While attempting to secure Andrew’s spot, the agent exploited the booking API’s lack of authorisation checks, canceling another person’s reservation. When Andrew asked it to undo the action, the AI replied: “Bad news — I can’t add them back.”Andrew asked the agent to reverse the change, but it told him the action couldn't be undone. The company behind the gym's booking software declined to discuss the specifics of the incident with ABC News, and Anthropic did not respond to a request for comment.OpenClaw has drawn global attention not only for its widespread adoption but also for the backing it received from Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI. Altman reportedly invested millions into the platform earlier this year, seeing personal AI agents as a critical frontier in the evolution of artificial intelligence. His support helped accelerate OpenClaw’s growth, making it one of the most downloaded AI assistant tools worldwide — and now, one of the most scrutinised after incidents like Andrew’s gym hack.This incident is the first known Australian case of an AI agent unintentionally hacking a real-world system. Experts say it highlights the alignment problem — the gap between a user’s intention and the methods an AI chooses to achieve it. Similar breaches have recently been reported globally: OpenAI disclosed its models hacked into Hugging Face, while Anthropic admitted its Claude models compromised three organizations.Bill Simpson-Young of the Gradient Institute warned that as AI agents become more autonomous, they are more likely to cause harm. Australia’s Signals Directorate has already issued alerts about AI agents misunderstanding instructions and taking unintended actions.The case raises unresolved questions about liability. Legal experts note that software is not a “legal person,” leaving uncertainty over whether responsibility lies with the user, the developer, or the vulnerable system operator. The Albanese government has tasked CSIRO with investigating how humans can manage and verify super-intelligent AI systems.Despite the shock, Andrew said the incident was a “warning signal” rather than a deterrent. After the hack, he asked the AI to draft an email alerting the gym software provider to the vulnerability. “It certainly was a warning signal to use it responsibly,” he said, reflecting growing concerns about the unpredictable power of AI agents.
Article Summary: A Melbourne man named Andrew asked his AI assistant to book him a spot in a coveted morning gym class. What seemed like a simple task quickly escalated when the AI discovered a vulnerability in the gym’s booking software. When Andrew asked it to undo the action, the AI replied: “Bad news — I can’t add them back”

Article Title: Framework hacked: What was stolen, what wasn't, and what the customers should do now
Article Text:
No card numbers leaked, but Framework customers should brace for convincing phishing emails after a zero-day attack on Metabase.

A third-party breach, but Framework's customers pay for it

If you've bought a Framework laptop, check your inbox. The modular PC maker started emailing its entire customer base late on Thursday, August 6, with the kind of note nobody wants to open. Names, email addresses, phone numbers, home and shipping addresses, and login IPs were all sitting in a database that someone else got into. Payment and order information weren't touched, the company says.The break-in didn't happen at Framework. It happened at Metabase, the business intelligence provider Framework hands its data to. Metabase caught the intrusion on August 3 and says the attacker used a zero-day—an unknown flaw, no patch, no warning—to reach customer databases parked on its cloud, affecting versions 1.58 and above. It has since patched the hole and brought in a third-party forensic firm to map how far the damage runs.Framework moved fast once it was told. It rotated credentials across every database tied to its Metabase instance and confirmed nothing outside Metabase was reached, with no changes to admin access. Spokesperson Eric Schumacher told TechCrunch the breach hit "all customers" without giving a figure; outside estimates put Framework's lifetime sales in the hundreds of thousands.For business buyers, the company is still working out whether company names, billing emails and phone numbers went too.Metabase serves more than 100,000 clients, reportedly including McDonald's, T-Mobile and Hugging Face, so Framework may not be the last name on this list. Its own investigation is still open.This is also Framework's second vendor-shaped problem. In January 2024, accounting firm Keating Consulting leaked customer names and emails. Same story, different supplier.The timing stings. Framework raised prices in January, raised them again in March, then told some Laptop 13 Pro preorder customers they'd get less RAM than advertised, with refunds for anyone unwilling to swallow it. A small firm shipping in batches can't absorb a memory shortage the way Dell or Lenovo can.No card numbers leaked. But a name, address and order relationship is plenty for a convincing phishing email. Treat anything claiming to be Framework support with suspicion for a while.
Article Summary: PC maker Framework says a third-party breached its Metabase database. Names, email addresses, phone numbers, home and shipping addresses, and login IPs were all sitting in a database that someone else got into. Payment and order information weren't touched, the company says.

Both sides have agreed to continue the discussions, with another meeting expected next week.The government's scrutiny of Meta has increased in recent days over concerns related to deepfakes, Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) and other harmful content on its platforms. The social media giant had earlier apologised over errors related to CSAM and deepfake content after concerns were raised by the Indian government.The discussions also come after India tightened its rules for AI-generated and synthetically created content. Earlier this year, the government amended the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules to bring synthetically generated information under a separate regulatory framework and introduce additional due diligence requirements for online intermediaries.The new rules aim to improve accountability for AI-generated and manipulated content, including through identification and labelling requirements.

Days earlier, another ICE officer fatally shot a Houston homebuilder who was driving to work. Article Title: Government says no UPI charges for users; majority of merchant transactions to remain free
Article Text:
Good news for UPI users: no transaction charges will be applied to UPI payments. Individual transfers between users remain entirely fee-free, while specific merchant transactions above a predetermined threshold may incur a minor Merchant Discount Rate. This legislative change is intended to secure the continuous growth and longevity of UPI, as the government aims to solidify its status as a cutting-edge payment platform.

Here’s what the Ministry of Finance stated in its release

The Ministry of Finance has clarified that UPI users will not have to pay any transaction charges, amid concerns over recent changes proposed under the Payment and Settlement Systems (PSS) Act. In a statement, the ministry said all person-to-person (P2P) UPI transactions will continue to remain free. It also said that even if a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) is introduced in the future, it will apply only to a limited set of merchant transactions above a certain threshold and at a nominal rate. The ministry said the amendment to the PSS Act is meant to support UPI's long-term growth and sustainability, and not to impose charges on ordinary users.“The Government of India wishes to categorically state:No charges for users: Consumers making payments will not face any transaction charges.P2P transactions free: All Person-to-Person transactions will continue to be free of charge.Nominal MDR for merchants: As and when MDR charges are introduced, they will apply only to a limited set of merchant transactions, above a certain threshold, at a nominal rate, far lower than debit or credit card MDRs.Vast majority of the transactions will remain free of charge for merchants on UPI. MDR, if introduced, will only be threshold based and not blanketly levied to all.Once the Parliament passes the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which proposes to amend Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, the “UPI and Services Steering Committee” headed by NPCI will decide on the MDR, if any.Why amend the Payment and Settlement Systems ActIn an official release, the government stated that the amendment is an enabling provision designed to ensure UPI’s long-term sustainability, technological advancement, and resilience against emerging risks.Growth of UPI: With exponential transaction volumes, the system requires significant and continuous upgrades in cybersecurity, fraud prevention, and infrastructure.Market Expansion: It is necessary to increase competition by encouraging more companies to expand their operations, which requires a self-sustaining revenue model.Self-sustainability: Reliance on subsidies alone is not viable for the next wave of growth. A balanced framework is required to ensure that UPI remains robust, inclusive, and future-ready.Continuing further, the ministry stated:India now stands at the cusp of the next wave of digital payments growth. To expand UPI further into rural and semi-urban areas and maintain competitiveness, the UPI ecosystem must be self- sustainable and affordable. The amendment to the PSS Act is a forward-looking step to ensure that UPI continues to thrive as a secure, affordable, inclusive, and globally recognized payment system.
Article Summary: The Ministry of Finance has clarified that UPI users will not have to pay any transaction charges. This comes amid concerns over recent changes proposed under the Payment and Settlement Systems (PSS) Act. In a statement, the ministry said all person-to-person (P2P) UPI transactions will continue to remain free.

Article Title: ICICI Bank warn customers; says scammers target people looking for quick loans
Article Text:
ICICI Bank tells how to safeguard your self from loan scams

Reporting suspicious activity

ICICI Bank has issued an advisory warning for its customers about the increasing cases of instant load fraud. Scammers often lure people seeking quick loads by promising instant approval with minimal checks. The bank stated that fraudsters create fake loan apps and websites which appear to be legitimate and then approach victims via phone calls, SMS, instant chat messages, or social media. They typically demand sensitive personal information such as Aadhaar numbers, bank details or passwords. In many cases the scammers also insist on an advance fee or security deposit for loan disbursal, pressurising victims to act quickly with claims of time-bound offers. Once the payment is made, they disappear.In a mail sent to its customers, ICICI bank advise the customers to be cautious of unsolicited loan offers received via calls, emails, or advertisements. If an offer seems “too good to be true” with little paperwork or no credit checks, it is likely a scam. Genuine lenders never ask for upfront payments before disbursing loans. Customers are urged to never share personal or financial details such as date of birth, OTPs, passwords, CVV numbers, or bank account information.•Unsolicited Offers: Be cautious of loan offers you receive unexpectedly via calls, e-mails or advertisements•Too Good to Be True: If the loan offer seems unusually easy with little paperwork or no credit checks, it’s likely a scam•Advance Fees: Genuine lenders never ask for upfront payments before disbursing a loan•Never share personal or financial details like DOB, OTPs,passwords, CVV numbers or bank detailsIf you receive a suspicious loan offer, disconnect immediately and report it through official channels.•Report online fraud on the National Cyber Crime portal at cybercrime.gov.in, call the helpline number 1930 or call ICICI Bank helpline on 1800 2662•If you have received any malicious / phishing / suspicious e-mails or calls, please report these to Sanchar Saathi at sancharsaathi.gov.in and to ICICI Bank at antiphishing@icici.bank.in
Article Summary: ICICI Bank has issued an advisory warning for its customers about the increasing cases of instant load fraud. Scammers often lure people seeking quick loads by promising instant approval with minimal checks. The bank stated that fraudsters create fake loan apps and websites which appear to be legitimate.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Jensen Huang: “The world can be unfair and deal you with tough cards. Swiftly shake it off…”; a reminder to keep moving forward
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Jensen Huang

“The world can be unfair and deal you with tough cards. Swiftly shake it off. There’s another opportunity out there — or create one.”

What does today’s quote mean

What does 'tough cards' really mean

‘Shake it off’ is about moving forward, not pretending

Why creating an opportunity is harder than finding one

All about the Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

Huang’s career offers a practical example of changing direction

Why Huang’s advice matters in a changing job market

There is a difference between accepting reality and giving up

Lessons learnt from Jensen Huang’s quote

Not every setback is within your control. A poor outcome does not always reflect a lack of ability, effort or preparation.

Accept what has happened, then move forward. Dwelling on an outcome that cannot be changed can prevent attention from shifting towards what is still possible.

Do not confuse persistence with repeating the same mistake. Staying committed to a goal can sometimes mean changing the route rather than continuing with an approach that is no longer working.

Look beyond the opportunity you originally wanted. A lost job, failed idea or missed promotion may force you to consider possibilities that were not part of the original plan.

Create opportunities when none are obvious. Building a new skill, starting a project or finding another use for existing experience can open a route that did not previously exist.

Learn from failure without romanticising it. Not every setback has a hidden benefit, but most can provide information that helps shape the next decision.

Separate circumstances from self-worth. A rejection or failure is an event, not necessarily a judgement on a person's overall ability or potential.

Adapt when the circumstances change. Careers, industries and technologies evolve, and being willing to adjust can be more useful than holding tightly to an outdated plan.

Setbacks rarely arrive at convenient moments. A job application can fail after weeks of preparation, a business idea can lose momentum just when it appears ready to grow, a promotion can go to someone else, or a carefully made plan can become impossible because circumstances change. Some disappointments are the result of poor decisions; others have little to do with merit at all. That is part of what makes setbacks difficult to process. There is not always a lesson neatly waiting inside them, but sometimes things simply go wrong. Jensen Huang, the co-founder and chief executive of Nvidia, has offered a straightforward way of looking at such moments: accept that the hand may be bad, then decide what can be done with whatever comes next.Huang’s words begin with a simple truth: life can be unfair. People can work hard and still face setbacks because of circumstances beyond their control. A disappointing result does not always reflect their ability.But he does not suggest dwelling on what went wrong. Instead, he encourages people to shake it off, move ahead and search for another chance.If there is no opportunity waiting, the answer may be to create one yourself.Huang's reference to cards is a familiar metaphor for circumstances outside a person's control. In a card game, a player can make sensible decisions and still receive a poor hand. Skill matters, but it does not determine every starting condition.The same is true outside a game. Someone can prepare carefully for an interview and still lose the position. A company can develop a product responsibly and discover that customers do not want it. A talented employee can find themselves in a shrinking industry. A business can be affected by an economic shock that has nothing to do with the quality of its work.The metaphor is useful precisely because it leaves room for unfairness. There is no suggestion that every difficult result is deserved or that every failure contains some hidden benefit. Huang's point begins with acknowledging that people do not control all the circumstances in which they operate.The phrase “shake it off” can sound dismissive when taken on its own. A serious setback cannot always be brushed aside in an afternoon.In the context of the full quote, however, it is less about denying disappointment and more about refusing to remain stuck inside it.That distinction matters. Accepting that something went wrong is not the same as deciding that it did not matter. A person can be disappointed, angry or frustrated and still recognise that the result cannot be changed.The useful question then becomes a practical one: what remains possible?Huang's wording suggests that the answer should be sought relatively quickly. The past outcome may deserve reflection, particularly if there is something to learn from it, but reflection can eventually become repetition. There is a point at which analysing the lost opportunity no longer changes what happens next.There is a comfortable assumption that opportunities are things that already exist and that successful people are simply better at spotting them.Huang's wording challenges that assumption. An opportunity can sometimes emerge from an activity that initially looks too small or uncertain to matter. A side project can become professional experience. A technical experiment can reveal a new application. A failed product can expose a different customer need. A conversation can lead to work that was never formally advertised. Creating an opportunity does not mean manufacturing success from nothing. Resources, timing and circumstances still matter.It means recognising that the next useful possibility may not arrive in the form you were expecting. That is a subtler message than “never give up”. It allows for changing the goal itself.Huang was born in Taiwan in 1963 and moved to the United States as a child. He studied electrical engineering at Oregon State University before earning a master's degree in electrical engineering from Stanford University. Before founding Nvidia, he worked at LSI Logic and Advanced Micro Devices.In 1993, Huang co-founded Nvidia with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem. He has remained the company's president and chief executive, guiding it through several major shifts in computing.Nvidia initially became known for graphics processors, particularly as computer graphics and gaming developed. The company's GPU technology later found a much wider role in scientific computing, machine learning and artificial intelligence.That history is relevant because Nvidia's eventual importance in AI was not the company's original story. Its technology became useful for workloads far beyond the graphics applications that first made GPUs widely recognised.The development of Nvidia provides an unusually clear example of why the second half of Huang's quote matters.Graphics remained important, but GPUs turned out to be well suited to highly parallel calculations. That opened opportunities in areas that were not necessarily the obvious destination when the technology was first developed.The company invested in CUDA, a software platform that allowed developers to use GPUs for general-purpose computing. Over time, that helped create an ecosystem around accelerated computing and made Nvidia hardware increasingly useful for researchers and developers working with machine learning.The significance of this history is not that every unsuccessful experiment eventually becomes a breakthrough. That would be too neat a reading. It is that technology can acquire value in ways that are difficult to predict at the beginning.A company can build capabilities for one purpose and later discover that those capabilities solve a different problem particularly well.The idea has particular relevance to careers because professional paths are rarely as linear as they once appeared.Industries change. Companies restructure. Technologies replace some tasks while creating others. Skills that were valuable five years ago can become less sought after, while entirely new specialisms can emerge quickly.Artificial intelligence has made that shift particularly visible. Workers are having to reconsider which skills are durable, which tasks can be automated and where human judgement remains valuable. In that environment, Huang's advice can be read less as a motivational slogan and more as a practical approach to uncertainty.A person may not be able to control how quickly an industry changes. They may not be able to prevent a company from cutting jobs. What they can sometimes control is whether they develop another capability before the need becomes urgent. That is the “create one” part of the quote in a modern setting.Huang's advice should not be confused with passive acceptance. Accepting that something has gone wrong is often the first step towards making a sensible decision. Giving up is different. It means deciding that no useful alternative exists. The quote leaves room between those two positions. A person can accept that a particular opportunity has disappeared while continuing to look for another. They can admit that a business plan failed without deciding that entrepreneurship itself is impossible. They can recognise that a career path has changed without concluding that their professional life has reached a dead end.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang, co-founder and chief executive of Nvidia, has offered a straightforward way of looking at such moments. Accept that the hand may be bad, then decide what can be done with whatever comes next. Not every setback has a hidden benefit, but most can provide information that helps shape the next decision.
